_about.one_line: The SovRing cores umbrella: Cores Studio (an offline local studio that routes prompts to spreadsheet, graphics, slide, voice and diagram cores, ingests files, searches your shard lake, runs a clean-room pipeline and bundles the results) with the doctor, math, embed, guard, redteam and core-models cores pinned as submodules.
_about.licence: PolyForm Small Business 1.0.0 / PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (LICENSING.md); PolyForm Free Trial for evaluation; documents CC BY 4.0
_about.stage: pre-alpha; studio about 30 %, doctor / math / embed submodules about 70 %
_about.source: tests/run-all.sh, tests/gui_smoke.py, tests/test_public_lake.py, each package's tests/; every row re-run on 2026-10-16 from a clean staged copy on an Intel i5-8365U laptop (results/)

tests.title: Every package's unit tests pass from a clean copy
tests.claim: xlsx-core 15, canva-core 11, slides-core 7, tts-core 12 (+1 skipped), diffusion-core 10, omniring_system 7, cores-studio 11 (+1 deselected), umbrella 3: all pass
tests.verify: bash -c 'T=$(mktemp -d) && tar --exclude=.git -cf - . | tar -xf - -C $T && cd $T && bash tests/run-all.sh | tail -1'
tests.what_it_means: Each of the seven packages runs its own unit tests from its own folder, plus the umbrella's tests, on a copy of the repository in a temporary directory. Passing means the spreadsheet engine evaluates formulas and writes valid workbooks, the graphics and slide cores render, the voice core turns text into phonemes and audio, the diagram core runs its integer forward pass, the abacus computes on its rings, and the studio's router, clean-room pipeline and core calls work, all without network access. It does not test the quality of what they produce for a human.
tests.how_we_got_it: bash tests/run-all.sh on a clean staged copy of this repository on 2026-10-16 (Intel i5-8365U laptop, Python 3.12.3, pytest 9.1.1); output in results/2026-10-16-run-all.log. The one deselected test needs the author's private concept graph (row S9); the skipped one needs the silk vocoder binary.
tests.use_in_your_work: A local toolkit you can trust to run offline: check it on your own machine in about 20 seconds before you rely on it for budgets, slides or narration.
tests.honest_limits: Unit tests check behaviour and structure, not output quality; speed claims in the cores' manuals were not re-measured.

tests.title: The studio runs end to end on 127.0.0.1 (page, ingestion, generation, clean room, shard lake, factory)
tests.claim: 6/6 steps: page served (85,938 bytes); a CSV + a Markdown file ingested; a prompt becomes a real .xlsx; the clean-room pipeline CERTIFIED (quality 100, 4 checks); shard search answers; factory ZIP with manifest.json (4 assets)
tests.what_it_means: The script starts the studio's web server from this checkout on a random free port bound to 127.0.0.1, then uses it the way the page does: loads the page, uploads two files, asks for a spreadsheet and downloads it (it must be a real OOXML ZIP with xl/workbook.xml), runs the clean-room pipeline on a directive, searches the shard lake and downloads the factory bundle (a ZIP whose manifest lists the session's assets). Then it stops the server. Passing proves the GUI's back end works from a clean clone with nothing installed but Python and numpy.
tests.how_we_got_it: python3 tests/gui_smoke.py on a clean staged copy, 2026-10-16, Intel i5-8365U laptop; output in results/2026-10-16-gui-smoke.log (one JSON line per step).
tests.use_in_your_work: Run the studio on a laptop with no internet: drop in a CSV of your sales or a Markdown plan and get a styled spreadsheet, a deck and a bundle you can hand to someone, with nothing leaving the machine.
tests.honest_limits: Checks that each feature answers correctly in structure; it does not judge the look of the artefacts. Session assets live in memory until the server stops.

tests.title: The shard lake searches a lake you make (fixture) and is empty when there is none
tests.claim: 3 passed: finds the note that contains the word, misses a word that is not there, returns [] when no lake exists
tests.verify: bash -c 'python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_public_lake.py 2>&1 | tail -1 | grep -o "3 passed"'
tests.what_it_means: The test writes a three-note SQLite lake in a temporary directory with the schema the studio reads (notes table plus an FTS5 full-text index), points the studio at it and searches. It shows the lake code works on your data and that a missing lake is handled as 'nothing found', not a crash. The author's own lake is private and is not part of this repository.
tests.how_we_got_it: tests/test_public_lake.py (pytest), run inside tests/run-all.sh on 2026-10-16 (results/2026-10-16-run-all.log, line 'umbrella tests/: 3 passed').
tests.use_in_your_work: Point the studio at a notes database of your own (recipes, repair logs, budgets) and turn a search hit into a spreadsheet or deck in one click, offline.
tests.honest_limits: A three-note fixture; search quality on a large lake is not measured here.

tests.title: Exact spreadsheet arithmetic: 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.3
tests.claim: xlsx-core evaluates formulas in exact decimal arithmetic and detects circular references (its 15 tests pass)
tests.verify: bash -c 'cd xlsx-core && python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_exact_math.py tests/test_formula_dag.py 2>&1 | tail -1 | grep -o "[0-9]* passed"'
tests.what_it_means: The spreadsheet core computes with decimal numbers, not binary floating point, so sums of money come out exactly (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3, not 0.30000000000000004), and it evaluates cells in dependency order, marking a circular reference instead of looping. The tests check those properties on fixed cases.
tests.how_we_got_it: The two test files run with pytest on 2026-10-16 inside tests/run-all.sh (results/2026-10-16-run-all.log, xlsx-core line).
tests.use_in_your_work: Household or small-business budgets and invoices where every cent must add up the same way every time.
tests.honest_limits: A subset of spreadsheet functions (SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, COUNT, PRODUCT, IF, ROUND, CONCAT, arithmetic, comparisons), not Excel's full library.

tests.title: The diamond abacus computes on 50 rings and matches plain integers
tests.claim: omniring_system: 7 tests pass (diamond cycle formulas on residues equal the integer results)
tests.verify: bash -c 'cd omniring_system && python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1 | tail -1 | grep -o "7 passed"'
tests.what_it_means: Four numbers are written onto four 50-ring residue systems (north, west, south, east), a formula is evaluated ring by ring with no carries, and the centre's result is read back and compared with the same formula on ordinary integers. Equality shows the abacus is exact for these formulas.
tests.use_in_your_work: A hands-on way to see residue-number arithmetic (the idea behind the Armilla Astrolabe) and to benchmark it on your own CPU from the studio's abacus tab.
tests.honest_limits: The Python abacus is a teaching and demo form; the fast kernels are in SovRing-Labs/armilla-astrolabe.

tests.title: The diffusion core's transformer is untrained (negative row)
tests.claim: diffusion-core's ternary DiT draws its weights from fixed pseudo-random seeds; no trained weights ship; diagrams come from topology templates
tests.verify: grep -q '_pseudo_random_ternary(seed' diffusion-core/diffusion_core/ternary_dit.py && grep -q 'diffusion-core does not learn' STATUS.md && echo untrained-stated
tests.what_it_means: This row exists so nobody mistakes the diagram core for a trained image model: the integer-only ternary forward pass is real and tested, but its weights are generated from fixed seeds, and the SVG diagrams are rendered from templates for each topology, filled from the prompt.
tests.how_we_got_it: Read from the source (ternary_dit.py: BitLinearLayer weights = _pseudo_random_ternary(seed, …)) on 2026-10-16.
tests.use_in_your_work: Use it for quick architecture diagrams from a prompt; use the forward pass as a readable reference for BitLinear layers.
tests.honest_limits: Training the DiT is not started.

tests.title: Air-gapped page: the GUI loads no remote resource
tests.claim: cores_studio/web/index.html references no http(s) host other than the SVG namespace URI
tests.verify: bash -c 'n=$(grep -o "https\?://[^\"[:space:])]*" cores-studio/cores_studio/web/index.html | grep -v "^http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" | wc -l); [ "$n" -eq 0 ] && echo no-remote'
tests.what_it_means: The studio page contains no link to a script, font, image or API on another host, so opening it never contacts the internet. Together with the 127.0.0.1 bind (S2) this is what 'offline' means here.
tests.how_we_got_it: grep over the shipped page on 2026-10-16: the only URLs are the SVG XML namespace (9 occurrences), which browsers do not fetch.
tests.use_in_your_work: Use it on a machine that must not leak data (clients' files, health or legal documents).
tests.honest_limits: Checks the page's text; it does not monitor the network at run time.

tests.title: The six engine cores are pinned at their release commits
tests.claim: .gitmodules lists doctor-core, math-core, embed-core, guard-core, redteam-core and core-models; each gitlink is that core's 0.1.0 release commit
tests.verify: bash -c 'n=$(git config -f .gitmodules --get-regexp "^submodule\..*\.url$" | grep -c "github.com/SovRing-Labs/"); [ "$n" -eq 6 ] && [ $(git ls-files -s | grep -c "^160000") -eq 6 ] && echo six-pinned'
tests.what_it_means: The umbrella records exactly which commit of each core it was tested with (a gitlink per submodule). A clone with --recursive gets those exact versions; a core upgrade is a visible one-line pin change.
tests.how_we_got_it: Written by the export tool when this release was cut (each core's own release commit), 2026-10-16.
tests.use_in_your_work: Reproducible setups: the same umbrella commit always means the same set of core versions.
tests.honest_limits: Needs a git checkout (not a source ZIP, which carries no gitlinks).

tests.title: Concept graph tab on the author's graph (external)
tests.claim: With the author's concept graph (83.9k nodes) the concept search, item, subgraph and multi-hop queries answer (cores-studio test_concept_graph_queries)
tests.verify: bash -c 'cd cores-studio && python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_studio_features.py -k concept_graph 2>&1 | tail -1'
needs: the author's data/shards/concept_graph.db and the concept-graph package (not in this release)
tests.what_it_means: The concept-graph tab reads a graph of concepts, their links and where each was seen. Building such a graph from your own documents needs a tool that is not part of this release, so this row only runs where that graph exists.
tests.how_we_got_it: The test passes in the author's development tree with the private graph present; it is deselected in tests/run-all.sh for everyone else.
tests.use_in_your_work: Once the graph builder is released: navigate your own notes by concept and find the shortest path between two ideas.
tests.honest_limits: Not runnable from a clean clone today.
